beats.say: A banana is an elongated, edible fruit that is botanically a berry produced by several kinds of large treelike herbaceous flowering plants in the genus Musa.
In some countries, cooking bananas are called plantains, distinguishing them from dessert bananas.
The fruit is variable in size, color and firmness, but is usually elongated and curved, with soft flesh rich in starch covered with a peel, which may have a variety of colors when ripe.
It grows upward in clusters near the top of the plant.
Almost all modern edible seedless (parthenocarp) cultivated bananas come from two wild species – Musa acuminata and Musa balbisiana, or their hybrids.
The story behind how bananas are technically radioactive is stranger than the version most people repeat.
The common explanation sounds right, but the measurements tell a different tale.
Researchers pinned it down by testing the obvious answer and watching it fail.
It comes down to simple physics, chemistry and a lot of time.
